correctness.rationale: The claimed minimum is correct. Equal-length squares are distinct and cannot contain each other. In any linear host, successive selected starts are separated by at least the least consistent positive overlap shift. Conversely, appending by those shifts preserves the whole new square at the suffix and all previously embedded factors. Adding the dummy creates a tour with cost 10 plus the shifts. Independently regenerated all costs and checked the literal 82-bit witness against all 32 factors. Rather than using the frozen numerical-optimality check as a proof, generated an independent binary branch certificate with valid directed cut inequalities. Each split fixes an arc bit to 0 or 1 and covers both cases. At each leaf, priced degree equalities and directed cut inequalities with the valid signs, then bounded each adjusted arc term by its exact minimum on its fixed value or on {0,1}. The standard-library replay verifies the result in integers: 557 splits, 558 leaves, 113 valid cuts, weakest rational lower bound 50659721/625000 > 81. Thus integral tour length is at least 82, and the witness attains it.
residual_risks: The independent exact certificate uses a different cut set and does not certify the particular floating-point solver run or the optimum of precisely the frozen 20-cut relaxation. It proves the actual linear minimum without that solver assumption.
